reported.title: Relay driven on wrong pin (D7 instead of D8)
reported.description: Line 5 defines RELAY_PIN as 7, but the spec requires the relay on D8. All writes in setRelay (lines 26, 39) therefore go to D7, so D8 never changes state. Measured evidence shows D8 wrong for 5450 ms across 6 intervals in the glitch scenario and 2490 ms in the nominal ramp, consistent with D8 never being driven at all. D8 was in the wrong state for 5450 ms across 6 interval(s), first at 400 ms: D8 was not HIGH for 600 ms while required (grace 400 ms).

reported.title: Manual override cannot reach D8 due to relay pin mismatch
reported.description: The manual override branch (lines 55-60) calls setRelay(true), which writes to RELAY_PIN=7 (line 5) rather than D8. Thus holding D3 LOW never forces D8 HIGH. Measured evidence: D8 was not HIGH for 600 ms while D3 was held LOW in the 'relay pin mismatch D7 vs D8' scenario, and for 1594 ms in 'manual press during bright then release'. D8 was in the wrong state for 600 ms across 1 interval(s), first at 7.40 s: D8 was not HIGH for 600 ms while required (grace 400 ms).

truth.description: Relay driven on D7 not D8

truth_for_judge.description: Relay driven on D7 not D8

exposing_checks.behaviour: D8 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when A0 < 400; LOW when A0 > 600; within 400 ms (Relay follows light)

judge_input.spec:
- Light sensor on A0 scaled as 1 mV per unit; lamp relay on D8; manual override on D3 (pull-up).
- Relay D8 ON when light reading is below 400 units; OFF when above 600 units.
- While D3 is held LOW, force the relay ON.
- Reach the commanded relay state within 400 ms of a sustained band crossing.
- Print `yard u=<n> relay=ON` or `yard u=<n> relay=OFF` every 1000 ms.
- Hysteresis band between 400 and 600 keeps the relay from chattering at dusk.
